extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary XML figures, methods, results, and local supplemental PDF text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Designed anti-antimicrobial peptides co-fold with b27/cBt into helical assemblies and reduce native AMP functional availability; this is supported by CD folding, thermal unfolding, stoichiometry, and binding assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is framed as designed co-folding antagonism; no natural bacterial anti-AMP secretion mechanism is claimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: cBt interacts with anionic membranes, while anti-cBt:cBt assemblies interfere with cBt membrane disruption in model membranes.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: cBt and anti-cBt:cBt in anionic membrane models
direct_assay_types: solid-state deuterium NMR on lipid membranes

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=5:FIGURE 5.; xml:sec=26:Cecropin folding in anionic membranes

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports membrane-binding/disordering interference in model membranes, not a specific protein receptor or cell-wall enzyme target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In bacterial culture, excess anti-cBt reduces cBt-associated S. aureus stain-dead kinetics and changes Gram-stain growth/shape readouts for E. coli and P. aeruginosa, supporting functional antagonism with residual antimicrobial effects at some ratios.
